title: Choosing a reptile species
steps: Research adult size, lifespan, diet, humidity and heating requirements before choosing a reptile.
Find an experienced exotic-animal vet and budget for electricity and equipment.
Prepare and test the enclosure before bringing an animal home.
caution: Reptiles have very different species-specific needs; do not use one generic setup.

title: Finding a reptile-experienced vet
steps: Locate a vet with reptile experience before an emergency.
Ask about routine checks and emergency availability.
Keep the practice number and transport container ready.
caution: Seek veterinary advice promptly for illness rather than relying on internet remedies.

title: Understanding captive-bred sourcing
steps: Choose a reputable breeder or rescue that can explain the animal's history.
Ask for feeding, shedding and health records.
Check legal ownership and documentation requirements for the species.
caution: Avoid wild-caught animals and never release unwanted reptiles.

title: Selecting an appropriately sized enclosure
steps: Research minimum adult enclosure dimensions for the exact species.
Allow room for a thermal gradient, hides and natural behaviours.
Check doors, ventilation and escape-proof locks.
caution: An enclosure suitable for a hatchling may be too small for an adult.

title: Building a temperature gradient
steps: Provide a warm basking zone and a cooler retreat suited to the species.
Measure both ends with reliable digital probes.
Adjust heat sources using appropriate thermostats.
caution: Never heat the whole enclosure to one uniform temperature.

title: Thermostat safety
steps: Connect suitable heating equipment to the correct type of thermostat.
Position probes according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Check readings and test the system before adding the animal.
caution: Uncontrolled heat sources can cause fatal overheating or burns.

title: Choosing safe basking lamps
steps: Choose an appropriate heat lamp and secure ceramic fitting.
Fit a guard where the animal could touch the bulb.
Check basking-surface temperatures with a suitable thermometer.
caution: Never allow direct contact with exposed hot bulbs.

title: Checking temperatures daily
steps: Read the warm and cool side temperatures each day.
Compare them with reliable species-specific care guidance.
Investigate sudden changes or faulty equipment promptly.
caution: An ambient room thermometer alone may not show basking-surface temperatures.

title: Understanding UVB needs
steps: Research the species' need for UVB lighting and exposure.
Select an appropriate reptile-rated lamp and mounting distance.
Follow manufacturer guidance for replacement and safe positioning.
caution: UVB requirements differ; glass and mesh can reduce effective exposure.

title: Planning a day-night light cycle
steps: Use a timer to create a consistent species-appropriate photoperiod.
Allow a proper dark period at night.
Avoid coloured night bulbs that disrupt normal behaviour.
caution: Heating after dark should not require visible light.

title: Monitoring humidity
steps: Use a reliable digital hygrometer at a representative location.
Adjust ventilation, water and substrate to the species' needs.
Watch for persistent condensation or excessively dry conditions.
caution: Too much or too little humidity can cause health problems.

title: Creating a humid hide
steps: For species that benefit, provide a sheltered hide with appropriately moist material.
Check it regularly for mould or fouling.
Let the animal choose between humid and dry areas.
caution: A humid hide is not a substitute for correct enclosure-wide conditions.

title: Safe water provision
steps: Provide clean water in a stable bowl sized for the animal.
Replace contaminated water promptly.
Clean the bowl with reptile-safe methods and rinse thoroughly.
caution: Water requirements vary; some species need misting or moving water.

title: Choosing safe substrate
steps: Research species-appropriate substrate and natural digging needs.
Avoid dusty, sharp or fragranced materials.
Spot-clean soiled areas and monitor for ingestion.
caution: Impaction risk depends on husbandry, health and substrate choice.

title: Providing multiple hides
steps: Place secure hides on both warm and cool sides.
Choose hides that fit the animal snugly but do not trap it.
Check them during routine cleaning.
caution: An exposed animal may be stressed even when temperatures are correct.

title: Securing branches and rocks
steps: Use stable, reptile-safe climbing branches and rocks.
Secure heavy decor so it cannot topple or collapse.
Check for sharp edges and pinch points.
caution: Unstable decor can crush or injure an animal.

title: Cleaning reptile enclosures safely
steps: Remove waste and soiled substrate promptly.
Use a disinfectant approved for reptile enclosures according to its label.
Rinse and dry items as directed before returning the animal.
caution: Never mix cleaning chemicals or use strong household sprays near reptiles.

title: Preventing salmonella spread
steps: Wash hands with soap after touching reptiles or enclosure items.
Keep reptile equipment away from food-preparation areas.
Supervise children and avoid kissing reptiles.
caution: Reptiles can carry Salmonella while appearing healthy.

title: Quarantining a new reptile
steps: Keep new reptiles separate from existing animals in a suitable enclosure.
Use dedicated tools and observe appetite, stools and behaviour.
Ask a reptile vet about testing and quarantine duration.
caution: Never introduce a new animal directly into a shared collection.

title: Reading reptile body language
steps: Observe posture, breathing, movement and hiding habits.
Learn normal behaviour for the exact species.
Reduce handling when the animal shows stress.
caution: A quiet reptile is not necessarily comfortable or healthy.

title: Gentle handling basics
steps: Allow a new reptile time to settle before handling.
Support its body securely and move slowly.
Keep sessions brief and species-appropriate.
caution: Avoid handling immediately after feeding or during distress.

title: Supervising children around reptiles
steps: Teach children to observe calmly and handle only with supervision.
Keep reptiles away from faces and mouths.
Wash hands thoroughly afterwards.
caution: Some reptiles are fragile, fast or capable of biting.

title: Recognising a normal shed
steps: Learn how often your species sheds and what healthy shedding looks like.
Check humidity, hydration and appropriate rubbing surfaces.
Observe eyes, toes and tail for retained skin.
caution: Do not forcibly peel skin; seek veterinary help for constricting retained shed.

title: Supporting a difficult shed
steps: Check enclosure temperatures and humidity against species guidance.
Provide an appropriate humid hide if suitable.
Contact a reptile vet for stuck shed around toes, eyes or tail.
caution: Avoid pulling retained skin or using unapproved oils.

title: Recording weight and growth
steps: Weigh the reptile using a secure container and suitable scale.
Record date, weight and feeding history.
Discuss unexpected weight changes with a reptile vet.
caution: Weight trends can reveal problems before they are obvious.

title: Keeping a feeding log
steps: Record food types, amounts, supplements and dates.
Note appetite changes and any regurgitation.
Review the log when planning veterinary visits.
caution: Sudden refusal to eat may require veterinary assessment.

title: Spotting urgent warning signs
steps: Watch for open-mouth breathing, severe lethargy, weakness or seizures.
Check equipment readings without delaying urgent care.
Contact a reptile-experienced vet promptly.
caution: Breathing difficulty, major injury or collapse is an emergency.

title: Recognising mouth problems
steps: Look for unusual drooling, swelling or refusal to eat.
Avoid forcing the mouth open or scraping lesions.
Arrange a reptile veterinary assessment.
caution: Mouth infections need diagnosis and treatment by a professional.

title: Understanding metabolic bone disease
steps: Review UVB, calcium, diet and heating for the species.
Watch for weakness, deformities or difficulty moving.
Seek reptile veterinary advice if signs are present.
caution: Do not attempt to correct suspected bone disease with supplements alone.

title: Managing suspected parasites
steps: Watch for unexplained weight loss, abnormal stools or persistent poor condition.
Keep records and request a reptile vet's advice on faecal testing.
Clean equipment according to veterinary instructions.
caution: Do not give dewormers intended for dogs or cats without a vet.

title: Planning an emergency power cut
steps: Keep safe temporary insulation and a backup power plan available.
Monitor enclosure temperatures during an outage.
Contact a vet or specialist if safe temperatures cannot be maintained.
caution: Avoid unventilated fuel heaters or placing hot packs directly against reptiles.

title: Transporting reptiles to the vet
steps: Use a secure ventilated container suitable for the species.
Maintain a safe temperature during travel without direct-contact heat sources.
Take husbandry records and recent photographs of the enclosure.
caution: Never leave a reptile in a parked vehicle.

title: Preventing escapes
steps: Inspect sliding doors, vents and cable openings regularly.
Use species-appropriate locks and secure lids.
Count and check animals before and after cleaning.
caution: Escaped reptiles can be injured or become dangerously cold.

title: Bearded dragon basking setup
steps: Provide an appropriate high-temperature basking spot with a cooler retreat.
Use suitable overhead UVB and verify its position.
Observe whether the dragon can move between zones easily.
caution: Follow current bearded-dragon-specific temperature and UVB guidance.

title: Bearded dragon salad choices
steps: Offer a varied selection of suitable leafy greens and vegetables.
Wash produce and remove spoiled leftovers.
Match insect feeding to age and veterinary nutrition guidance.
caution: Avoid relying on iceberg lettuce or fruit-heavy diets.

title: Bearded dragon insect feeding
steps: Choose appropriately sized, captive-raised feeder insects.
Gut-load feeders and use supplements according to reptile-vet advice.
Remove uneaten live insects when needed.
caution: Do not collect insects from areas treated with pesticides.

title: Leopard gecko hide arrangement
steps: Provide warm, cool and moist hides in a secure enclosure.
Check that hides are easy to enter and exit.
Monitor how the gecko uses each area.
caution: Leopard geckos still need a species-appropriate heat gradient and lighting.

title: Leopard gecko feeding routine
steps: Offer suitable live insects of an appropriate size.
Use a species-appropriate calcium and vitamin schedule.
Record appetite and weight changes.
caution: Never leave large live insects unattended where they may bite the gecko.

title: Leopard gecko tail safety
steps: Support the body gently and avoid grabbing the tail.
Provide calm hiding spaces to reduce stress.
Seek veterinary help for injury or a dropped tail.
caution: A dropped tail can regrow differently; never try to pull it off.

title: Crested gecko vertical habitat
steps: Provide a tall enclosure with secure branches and foliage.
Create suitable temperature and humidity cycles.
Ensure ventilation and safe landing areas.
caution: Crested geckos can overheat in temperatures suited to desert reptiles.

title: Crested gecko prepared diet
steps: Use a complete commercially formulated crested gecko diet as directed.
Provide fresh water and remove old food promptly.
Ask a specialist about any supplemental insects.
caution: Fruit alone is not a balanced long-term diet.

title: Corn snake enclosure security
steps: Use a well-ventilated, escape-proof enclosure with secure doors.
Provide warm and cool hides and appropriate substrate.
Check locks after every feeding and cleaning session.
caution: Snakes can squeeze through small gaps.

title: Corn snake feeding safety
steps: Offer appropriately sized, safely thawed frozen prey using feeding tongs.
Follow species- and age-appropriate feeding intervals.
Allow the snake to digest undisturbed.
caution: Do not feed live rodents or microwave frozen prey.

title: Ball python humidity and hides
steps: Provide snug hides on both ends of a temperature gradient.
Monitor species-appropriate humidity and ventilation.
Record shedding and feeding patterns.
caution: Ball pythons may become stressed without secure hides.

title: Ball python feeding refusal
steps: Review temperature, security, recent handling and shedding.
Record how long the animal has refused food and monitor weight.
Consult a reptile vet if weight falls or illness is suspected.
caution: Do not repeatedly offer prey or force-feed without veterinary guidance.

title: Tortoise outdoor security
steps: Research whether the species can safely use outdoor space in your climate.
Provide secure boundaries, shelter and predator protection.
Check for toxic plants and escape routes.
caution: Different tortoise species have very different climate needs.

title: Tortoise diet variety
steps: Identify the tortoise species before planning its diet.
For grazing species, offer suitable weeds and leafy plants with appropriate fibre.
Seek specialist advice on calcium and UVB provision.
caution: Fruit-rich diets are unsuitable for many commonly kept tortoises.

title: Tortoise hibernation decisions
steps: Confirm the exact species and whether brumation is appropriate.
Arrange a reptile-vet health check and species-specific plan.
Never attempt hibernation without reliable guidance.
caution: Some tortoise species must not hibernate; unsafe temperatures can be fatal.

title: Aquatic turtle basking access
steps: Provide a fully dry, easy-to-reach basking platform.
Position suitable heat and UVB lighting safely above it.
Keep the water clean with adequate filtration.
caution: Turtles must be able to dry completely while basking.

title: Aquatic turtle water quality
steps: Use filtration sized for the species and water volume.
Test water quality and perform regular conditioned water changes.
Keep electrical equipment secure and protected from splashes.
caution: Turtles produce substantial waste and can outgrow small tanks.

title: Species-specific cohabitation
steps: Research whether your reptile species is naturally solitary.
Provide separate enclosures unless a qualified specialist advises otherwise.
Watch for competition over heat, hides and food.
caution: Many reptiles should not be housed together, even if they appear calm.

title: Planning lifelong reptile care
steps: Check expected lifespan and adult housing costs.
Arrange trusted care for holidays and emergencies.
Keep written feeding, heating and veterinary instructions.
caution: Some reptiles live for decades and require long-term specialist care.
